about.title: A small window into a public dataset.
paragraphs: This dashboard is built from the HATVP open-data pipeline. The pipeline preserves raw source files, normalizes records, checks quality, and publishes four Gold BigQuery tables.
The overview intentionally exposes aggregates only. Personal contact details and raw declaration rows are not part of this public API.

The dashboard combines three clearly labelled source streams. The HATVP website is the official, current publication. The Internet Archive's Wayback Machine and the companion GitHub archive preserve earlier public declarations that HATVP has since unpublished. A separate static Hugging Face snapshot, assembled by thefrenchartist, provides another preserved copy of historical declaration XML. These recovery sources help preserve public history for comparison and research; they are not new HATVP publications.
about.sourcePrefix: For the authoritative current publication and the full declaration context, use the official HATVP links below.

what.question: What is this dashboard?
what.answer: A reader-friendly view of public HATVP declarations. It helps you move from a dated aggregate to the declaration and source that support it.

snapshot.question: Which snapshot am I seeing?
snapshot.answer: Each page labels the latest successful snapshot date and generation time beside claims that depend on the data.

counted.question: How are values counted?
counted.answer: Counts and amounts follow the documented Gold tables and metric eligibility rules. Reported years, observed assets, and missing values keep their source meaning.

preserve.question: What does the pipeline preserve?
preserve.answer: Raw bytes, source identifiers, provenance, historical versions, and review flags are retained so a reader can inspect the publication history.

source.question: Where can I inspect the source?
source.answer: Use the official HATVP links for the current publication. Archived copies are labelled separately and link back to their archive provenance.

notIncluded.question: What is not included?
notIncluded.answer: The public aggregate API does not expose contact details or addresses. Review flags are signals for inspection, not proof of an error or misconduct.

archive.title: Why Wayback declarations appear here.
archive.description: The Wayback Machine preserves earlier public versions of HATVP declaration pages and XML files. YAHATVP uses that archive to recover declarations the official site has since withdrawn, while keeping their provenance visible and their status separate from current HATVP publication.

huggingFace.title: A static snapshot made by thefrenchartist.
huggingFace.description: YAHATVP also ingests a static historical snapshot of HATVP declaration XML published on Hugging Face by thefrenchartist, the author of this project. It is not a live feed: the pipeline downloads the archive, extracts and normalizes the XML, deduplicates declarations, and keeps the source provenance visible.

explore.title: The declarations worth a closer look.
explore.description: Current review leads from the latest public snapshot. Income cards use the latest declaration version and current anomaly-registry signals. Every record links back to the source.
explore.incomeDescription: The biggest absolute changes between consecutive completed years in each declarant’s latest declaration. Only changes linked to current anomaly-registry records are shown; source values are preserved exactly.
explore.incomeMeaning: This is a comparison between consecutive reported years. The review label reflects a current statistical signal; it is not a finding that the source amount is wrong.
explore.assetsDescription: Up to 10 of the highest reported values from the miscellaneous-assets section of current public declarations. These are source-declared values in this snapshot, not a complete measure of wealth.
explore.assetsMeaning: This ranking keeps the source-declared item and value together. A high amount is context for reading a declaration and is not evidence of misconduct.
explore.amendedDescription: Declarants with the largest number of amended filings in retained Silver history. A high count is context for investigation; it does not imply that a declaration was incorrect.
explore.amendedMeaning: An amendment is a later public version kept as part of publication history. A count helps you inspect the record’s history and does not establish an error.

simpleAnalysis.title: Age, pay, and the shape of the dataset.
simpleAnalysis.description: A first statistical view of public declarants. Unusual ages stay visible and are labelled rather than hidden.
simpleAnalysis.emptyLeaders: No parsed dates of birth are available in this snapshot.
simpleAnalysis.salaryDescription: Average and median normalized declarant income, grouped by age at the income year. Active income anomalies are excluded from the statistics but retained in the source-linked tables.
simpleAnalysis.ageFilterNote: Age range: 18–100. Only rows with a usable date of birth and income year are included.
simpleAnalysis.salaryMeasureNote: Average and median reported salary are different measures.
simpleAnalysis.emptySalary: No eligible salary rows have a usable DOB and year.
simpleAnalysis.chartLabel: Average and median salary by five-year age bin
simpleAnalysis.zeroSalaryDescription: Count of declarations with a normalized 0€ salary in each five-year age bin. The age window is limited to 18–100 for this analysis.
simpleAnalysis.emptyZeroSalary: No 0€ salary rows have a usable DOB and year.
simpleAnalysis.zeroSalaryChartLabel: Count of 0€ salary declarations by five-year age bin
simpleAnalysis.anomalyNote: Anomaly labels are signals for review, not corrections to the published DOB.

ageAnalysis.title: Read one declarant’s latest story — with its history intact.
ageAnalysis.description: Income comes from the newest interest declaration; assets come from the newest patrimonial declaration. Earlier versions remain available for audit.
ageAnalysis.hint: Search is accent-insensitive and uses public fields from the latest normalized snapshot.
ageAnalysis.contextDescription: The primary view never adds amended and earlier filings together. It selects the newest interest declaration for income and the newest patrimonial declaration for the asset inventory.
ageAnalysis.historyDescription: Earlier filings are preserved for comparison. Only entries marked selected contribute to the primary income or asset view.
ageAnalysis.incomeDescription: Roles, employers, periods, and annual amounts are read together from the newest interest declaration. Totals reproduce the published source values without correction.
ageAnalysis.reviewWarningTitle: These amounts are flagged for review
ageAnalysis.reviewWarningDescription: They are shown unchanged because this detail view is for source inspection. They remain excluded from aggregate metrics while their review flags are active.
ageAnalysis.noIncome: No annual income was published in the selected interest declaration.
ageAnalysis.assetEyebrow: One item per latest patrimonial declaration
ageAnalysis.assetDescription: Each current asset appears once, including accounts with no event date. Values come from the newest patrimonial declaration and are not summed across versions.
ageAnalysis.assetDateClarification: An asset date describes an acquisition, subscription, or holding event. It is not the year when the declaration was filed.
ageAnalysis.noEventDate: No acquisition or subscription date was published.
ageAnalysis.minorPolicyNote: A subscription before age 18 is not automatically an error: a legal representative may manage a minor’s life-insurance policy.
ageAnalysis.noAssets: No assets were published in the selected patrimonial declaration.
ageAnalysis.loadError: This declarant analysis could not be loaded.

qualityIssues.title: Issues reported to HATVP.
qualityIssues.description: A public, redacted register of data-quality issues raised with HATVP. It contains only issue types, contact dates, public HATVP links, and resolution status.
qualityIssues.privacyNote: Emails, message contents, and HATVP replies are intentionally excluded from this page.

pipelineHealth.title: The data pipeline, in view.
pipelineHealth.description: Track the latest run, source coverage, layer quality, and records that need review. The pipeline combines the current official HATVP publication with two separately labelled historical Wayback recovery archives.
pipelineHealth.flaggedDetail: High-level count of records carrying an active quality or anomaly signal.
pipelineHealth.sourcesDescription: The HATVP website is the official publication and weekly refresh. The GitHub / Wayback and HF / Wayback archives are historical recovery streams: HATVP can unpublish declarations after a person leaves public office, so archived records extend historical coverage without being mistaken for current official publication.
pipelineHealth.qualityTitle: Rows and review load by layer
pipelineHealth.policyDescription: Asset rows are currently treated as anomaly-free for public metrics: compensation-oriented anomaly rules are disabled for assets. For incomes, COMP_YOY_CHANGE and COMP_DIGIT_EDIT are temporarily ignored because they generated too many false positives; all other income anomaly rules still exclude affected values. Source rows and historical evidence remain preserved for later review.
